note: From the Valencia County Clerk's 2026 General Election Notice of Election, which lists the offices, qualified candidates and questions on the county's ballot. The New Mexico Secretary of State's candidate portal was offline for maintenance on 2026-11-03. Not shown because they depend on where you live: County Commission Districts 1 and 3, U.S. House districts 1, 2 and 3, State House districts 7, 8, 49 and 69, and the Public Education Commission district. Statewide races, Supreme Court and Court of Appeals retention, constitutional amendments and state bond questions appear with the New Mexico statewide ballot. The county seat, Los Lunas, has no village contest or question on this notice. Incumbency is marked only for judges standing for retention. Names appear as printed in the notice. Check your official sample ballot.

measures.title: Valencia County Sheriff and Fire Facilities Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether Valencia County may issue up to $1,000,000 in general obligation bonds, repaid from property taxes. The money would be used to build, renovate, furnish and otherwise improve buildings for sheriff and fire department facilities.
measures.yesMeans: The county may issue up to $1,000,000 in property-tax-backed bonds for sheriff and fire department buildings.
measures.noMeans: The county may not issue these bonds for sheriff and fire department buildings.

measures.title: Valencia County Road Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether Valencia County may issue up to $4,000,000 in general obligation bonds, repaid from property taxes. The money would be used to build, rehabilitate and otherwise improve public roads, including buying capital equipment for those projects.
measures.yesMeans: The county may issue up to $4,000,000 in property-tax-backed bonds for public roads.
measures.noMeans: The county may not issue these bonds for public roads.

measures.title: Valencia County Parks and Recreation Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether Valencia County may issue up to $2,000,000 in general obligation bonds, repaid from property taxes. The money would be used to build, equip, renovate and improve park and recreational facilities, including public parks, splash pads, sports fields, open space, bike paths, Bosque lands and trails.
measures.yesMeans: The county may issue up to $2,000,000 in property-tax-backed bonds for park and recreational facilities.
measures.noMeans: The county may not issue these bonds for park and recreational facilities.

measures.title: Valencia County Community Center Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether Valencia County may issue up to $2,000,000 in general obligation bonds, repaid from property taxes. The money would be used to build, equip, renovate and improve county-owned community centers, including those for families, youth and senior citizens.
measures.yesMeans: The county may issue up to $2,000,000 in property-tax-backed bonds for county-owned community centers.
measures.noMeans: The county may not issue these bonds for county-owned community centers.
